rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse directs attention to a divine favor and guides people toward the duties and aims that follow from it.
rows.anchor: insanlara olan lütuflarından birine tenbih ve ona müterettib vazife ve gayelerine irşaddır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fronting “for you” marks particularization: Earth is made compliant for humans, especially the rational hearers addressed, rather than for every creature indiscriminately.
rows.anchor: ihtisas ifade eder. Yani her şey ve her mahluk için değil, ancak siz insanlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zelûl is an intensive adjective from zill, the verbal noun of submission, and describes something made compliant and readily usable as one wishes.
rows.anchor: “Zelûl”, inkıyad demek olan, kesr ile, “zill” masdarından mübalağa vasfıdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Compliance here means ease, softness, suitability, and docility, rather than disgrace; a compliant thing may still possess honor.
rows.anchor: Bunda aslolan hakāret ve horluk mânası değil, kolaylık, yumuşaklık, uygunluk,

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His couplet presents humility before God as a means of elevation and honor, illustrating that docility need not entail humiliation.
rows.anchor: Hâk ol ki Hudâ mertebeni eyleye âlî

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zelîl, by contrast, means contemptible or abject and derives from zull with a damma, unlike zelûl from zill.
rows.anchor: hakir demek olan “zelîl” zâlin zammıyla “züll” masdarından gelir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Animal examples distinguish docility from disgrace: sheep and camels are yielding without being abject, while a donkey exemplifies both qualities.
rows.anchor: Koyun zelûldür, zelil denilmez. Eşek zelûl olmakla beraber zelil olmakta da meseldir. Deve zelûldür, zelil değildir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He further distinguishes trained horses, workhorses, mules, and difficult rocks by whether they are compliant, abject, or neither.
rows.anchor: At ehline zelûldür. Ufak bir işaretten anlar, zelil değildir. Kullanmasını bilmeyeni dinlemez, silker geçiverir. Beygir de hem zelûl hem zelildir. Katır zelildir, pek zelûl değildir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qurʾānic description of livestock as subdued for human use illustrates the same sense of docility.
rows.anchor: وَذَلَّلْنَٰهَا لَهُمْ فَمِنْهَا رَكُوبُهُمْ وَمِنْهَا يَأْكُلُونَ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling Earth zelûl is a simile, like describing a compliant animal; things as difficult to use as stone would only be called zelûl metaphorically.
rows.anchor: Arz’a zelûl ıtlakı teşbîhîdir. كَحَيـَوَانٍ ذَلُولٍ demek gibidir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the command says to walk on its shoulders, Earth is likened to a ridden horse or camel, most readily an Arabian horse or hejin, rather than merely an animal used for food or milk.
rows.anchor: Menâkibinde meşy emri karînesiyle bunun sade bir koyun gibi eti yenir, sütü sağılır, yünü kırpılır değil, at veya deve gibi daha ziyade binilmesi mu‘tad olan en mühim bir hayvana teşbih edilmiş olduğu anlaşılıyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earth is pictured as a mount that yields to every use, carries its riders gently, and moves so smoothly and quickly that its motion scarcely shakes them.
rows.anchor: uysal bir binit hâlinde tasvir olunmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The image also conveys that God presents Earth’s actual movement as imperceptible to people.
rows.anchor: Allah teâlâ bize Arz’ın hareketini vâki‘de olduğu gibi gayr-i mahsüs bir hâlde bildirmiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contextual clues that reinforce a simile or metaphor are called tarshīḥ; the mount image is reinforced by the wording about walking on its shoulders.
rows.anchor: teşbih ve istiareleri takviye eden karînelere “terşih”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command has two senses: people walk on Earth within its bounds, with “in” attached to walking and “shoulders” as the place traversed.
rows.anchor: Birisi onun üzerinde, omuzları içinde yürümektir ki bu bildiğimiz vechile Arz üzerinde bizim bizzat yürüyüşümüzdür.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, as with travel on a horse or ship, Earth itself walks by God’s command while people travel indirectly on its back; the next verse’s reference to heaven signals this movement toward the sky.
rows.anchor: Bunda Allah teâlâ’nın emriyle evvelen ve bizzat yürüyen Arz, saniyen onun üzerinde olarak bi’l-vâsıta yürüyen de biz olmuş oluruz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Menkib means shoulder, but the plural menâkib rather than “two shoulders” implies that Earth has many such shoulders, prompting inquiry into their referent.
rows.anchor: Fakat görülüyor ki في مَنْكِبـَيـْهَا yani iki omuzu denilmemiş, cemi‘sîgasıyla “menâkib” buyurulmuştur.

rows.speaker: قتادة والضحاك وابن عباس
rows.claim: They interpret Earth’s shoulders as its mountains and hills, elevated like human shoulders; ease even across these least-yielding parts implies still greater ease elsewhere.
rows.anchor: Katâde ve Dahhâk ve İbn Abbas’ın kavlidir ki Arz’ın menâkibi cibâl ve âkâmı, yani dağları ve tepeleri

rows.speaker: Hasan, Mücâhid, Kelbî, Mukātil, Atâ, İbn Abbas, Ferrâ, İbn Kuteybe
rows.claim: They interpret Earth’s shoulders as its roads, openings, surrounding regions, and sides; Ferrā and Ibn Qutayba prefer this view, which is compared to Noah 71:19–20.
rows.anchor: Bu da Hasan’ın, Mücâhid’in, Kelbî’nin ve Mukātil’in kavli ve Atâ’nın İbn Abbas’tan rivayeti ve Ferrâ’nın ve İbn Kuteybe’nin muhtârlarıdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountains-and-hills and roads-and-sides interpretations both treat “shoulders” as a word-level metaphor.
rows.anchor: Bu iki kavilde “menâkib”de mecâz fi’l-müfred var demektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In his rendering of the warning, he describes Earth as swallowing its inhabitants.
rows.anchor: sizinle Arz’ı göçürüvermesinden

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He renders the threatened heavenly sender as one who rains down projectiles upon people.
rows.anchor: üzerinize bir mermiler yağdırıcı gönderivermesinden

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He renders the warning about earlier deniers as a question about how his punishment or retribution came to pass.
rows.anchor: fakat nasıl oldu inkârım

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His rendering depicts birds above as gliding with wings extended and then folding them, with the Merciful alone sustaining them.
rows.anchor: kanat süzerlerken ve yumarlarken? Rahman’dır ancak onları tutan

rows.speaker: Sâhib-Keşşâf
rows.claim: Walking on a camel’s shoulders is proverbial hyperbole for maximal subjugation: the shoulders and neck base are too thin and unsuitable to bear a rider’s foot.
rows.anchor: Sâhib-Keşşâf demiştir ki: “Omuzlarda yürümek tâbiri fart-ı tezlîlde meseldir.

rows.speaker: Sâhib-Keşşâf
rows.claim: If a camel could be walked upon at its shoulders, it would have reached the utmost degree of obedience and submission; Earth’s “shoulders” similarly imply extreme docility.
rows.anchor: Sâhib-Keşşâf demiştir ki: “Omuzlarda yürümek tâbiri fart-ı tezlîlde meseldir. Çünkü iki omuz ve onların mültekāsı olan ense kökü devenin en ince

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this reading, the command is a metonymy for Earth being so compliant that people may use it as they wish; he calls the interpretation good.
rows.anchor: Bu surette فَٱمْشُوا۟ فِى مَنَاكِبِهَا Arz’ın zelûliyette nihâyet derecede olmasından kinaye olarak “onda istediğiniz gibi tasarruf edin” demek olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He argues the metaphor alone may not encourage searching out Earth’s shoulders, whereas the command’s exploratory force helped Muslims spread through the world in a short time.
rows.anchor: bu emir, Arz üzerinde inkişaf hissini

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Synthesizing the three readings, he takes Earth’s shoulders to mean its entire surface, including the highest, most distant, difficult, and delicate places, from mountains and valleys to all directions and poles; the “sides” reading is broadest.
rows.anchor: Arz’ın menâkibi Arz’ın en yüksek, en uzak ve yürümek için en müşkil ve en nâzik yerlerine kadar sırtı demek olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If walking is generalized to all possible uses, the image also includes searching underground through excavation, rather than remaining on the surface.
rows.anchor: hafriyyât vesâire suretiyle derinliklerinde taharrî mânası da anlaşılır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Walking Earth’s shoulders first requires discovering and understanding it through geography, which reports the conditions of its surface.
rows.anchor: Arz’ın menâkibinde yürümek için evvelemirde onu keşfedip bilmeye de ihtiyaç vardır. Bu ise Arz’ın sathî ahvâlini bildiren ve coğrafya denilen mâlumat ile olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse encourages learning geography, advancing discoveries, and verifying, improving, and recording them, as well as pursuing practical sciences through Earth research.
rows.anchor: o ilmi tahsîle ve peyderpey keşfiyyâtı ileri götürerek tahkik ve ıslah ile tedvîne dahi bir teşvik vardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although exegetes generally classify walking and eating as permissions, the context presents guidance between divine favor and warning, so the commands exceed bare permission.
rows.anchor: siyâk-ı kelâm bu emirlerin mücerred ibâha için değil, lütf u inzar beyninde bir irşad için olduğunu göstermektedir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As favor, the commands encourage action through God-given capacity and may mean recommendation or obligation; securing food and enough to avoid death is obligatory.
rows.anchor: Nafakasını tedarik etmek ve ölmeyecek kadar yemek vâcib olduğu cihetle bu gibi ahvâlde bu emirler ibâha hâlinde kalamaz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As warning, “to Him is the resurrection” directs people to work and eat remembering their giver, death, and accountability, avoiding injustice, aggression, extravagance, and debauchery.
rows.anchor: Allah’ı ve ölümü unutmayarak ve O’na hesap vereceğinizi düşünerek hareket edin.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taken together, the commands remain generally permissive but give important individual and social guidance; ijtihād must distinguish obligation, recommendation, and permission by circumstance.
rows.anchor: ahvâlin iktizâsına göre vücub, nedb, ibâha hükümlerini bi’l-ictihâd ayırmak îcab eder.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Walking and eating connect labor and good conduct in the struggle for livelihood; this also explains reports that reciting the sūrah is associated with abundant provision.
rows.anchor: bu meşyin rızık işi, yani hayat mücadelesinde hüsn-i amel ile sa‘y ü kesb meselesine ta‘allukunu ifade eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse gives a practical picture of life and death as a testing ground for the best deeds described earlier.
rows.anchor: mevt ve hayat arasında ahsen-i amel için imtihan meydanına çıkışın amelî bir manzarasını anlatmış olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to walk is tied to livelihood obligations and covers all means of earning, including fighting, trade, agriculture, and industry.
rows.anchor: bu meşy emri bir mükellefiyet ile alâkadar olarak rızık kesbi esbâbından hepsine şâmil olmak üzere mülâhaza olunmak iktizâ eyler.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commands also include spiritual benefits: observing and studying the horizons for insight and knowledge, and spreading religion and virtue to earn reward, as in the cited travel commands.
rows.anchor: âfâkı müşahede ve tedkik ile ibret ve marifet tahsil etmek ve din ve fazilet neşri ile kesb-i mesûbât eylemek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though addressed to individuals too, the commands especially concern society collectively; Muslims are sent into the testing ground to compete in good works.
rows.anchor: emirler aynen ferdlere dahi hitab olmakla beraber daha ziyade kifaye suretiyle cemiyete müteveccihtir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Eat” is a specific expression for general benefit and includes drinking, clothing, and other forms of use, while provision includes immaterial goods too.
rows.anchor: ekl, yalnız yiyeceğe mahsus olmayıp zikr-i hâs irâde-i âm kabîlinden olarak şürb,

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Provision encompasses immaterial things such as knowledge, as indicated by the verse in al-Baqara about spending from what God provides.
rows.anchor: kavlinde geçtiği üzere rızık da maddiyâttan başka ilim gibi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A well-known theological definition describes provision as what God conveys to animals for them to eat, explaining eating in terms of receiving benefit.
rows.anchor: diye meşhur olan târifte ekl

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Provision is not confined to Earth: its most important basis is in heaven, and al-Baqara 2:29 also directs attention to heaven after creation of what is on Earth.
rows.anchor: rızkımızın en mühim esası semâda olmasına

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As people walk Earth, they also travel toward heaven, receiving air, light, and other material and spiritual descents through known and unknown means.
rows.anchor: Arz’ın omuzlarında yürürken yalnız Arz’da değil, onunla beraber semâya doğru da

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Therefore work and eating should be pursued with alertness and a lofty purpose: good intention for God, concern for the afterlife, and a place in His dominion.
rows.anchor: binâen‘aleyh bu meşy ve eklin gafletle ve süfliyetle değil, büyük bir intibah ve yüksek bir hayat gayesiyle yapılması lâzım gelir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nushūr can mean spreading but chiefly means life, especially life after death, or resurrection; people must remember that their endpoint is a return to their origin and resurrection to God.
rows.anchor: “nüşûr” intişar mânasına da gelmekle beraber daha ziyade hayat ve bâhusus ölümden sonra hayat, ta‘bîr-i âharla ba‘s demektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is both the beginning and the end; all journeys form a circular motion joining their two ends, and He continually holds their reins.
rows.anchor: Evvel O olduğu gibi nihâyet Âhir de O’dur. Bütün seyirler, yürüyüşler böyle iki ucu birleşen bir daire üzerinde bir hareket-i deverâniye demektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Life and its purpose belong to God, the sovereign; those who ignore the unity of origin and return become lost, and the highest ideal must be His pleasure.
rows.anchor: Asıl hayat ve gāye-i hayat sizin değil O’nundur. Bi-yedihi’l-mülk O’dur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whatever people pursue, they will arrive before God carrying responsibility for their intentions; mortal aims fade, while what accords with the enduring order remains.
rows.anchor: o niyet ve maksadın mes’ûliyetini hâmil olarak varacaksınız. Fâni maksadlar sönecek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who kindle Hell through evil deeds go to Hell, while those who beautify Paradise through good deeds attain forgiveness and Paradise.
rows.anchor: Kötü amellerle sa‘îri körükleyenler sa‘îre, güzel amellerle cenneti süslemeye çalışanlar mağfiret ve cennete erecektir.
